record.title: Zero-valued MMIO can fabricate device presence
record.method: Mixed-board restore-stage observation and source/disassembly comparison
record.observation: A phone restore-stage diagnostic running on the iPod QEMU model reported a radio board in a model without a radio. The relevant input defaulted to zero, which the diagnostic interpreted as presence.
record.limits: This is a false positive about a detection predicate, not evidence of a working modem or a complete iPhone profile.

records.access: Private project record; original material is not distributed

exhibits.title: A specific address explains the false detection
exhibits.interpretation: The zero value satisfies the firmware’s presence predicate. The QEMU model has no radio; the observation demonstrates a false positive in the model contract.

exhibits.title: Interpret the predicate, not the message
exhibits.interpretation: The nonzero row describes the inspected branch, not an executed negative-control run. Explicitly separating those evidence types prevents a second unsupported claim.

excerpts.content:
The read helper selects GPIO bank 7, bit 1: it reads a word at `0x3e400004 + 7 * 0x20 = 0x3e4000e4` and tests mask `0x2`. A zero result takes the branch to the radio-present message at `0x18000ed4`; a nonzero result prints that no radio board was detected.

[…]

The pinned QEMU `hw/arm/ipod_touch_gpio.c` handles only offset `0x2c4` in its read callback and returns zero for every other GPIO offset. Its write callback ignores all writes. Thus the read at offset `0xe4` supplies the low bit value that this iBEC interprets as an installed radio board. This explains the existing console observation without implying a working baseband.
